newsitem.title: JAPAN: RUBBER-JAPAN PRICES SEEN IN RANGE, TRADE LETHARGIC.
newsitem.headline: RUBBER-JAPAN PRICES SEEN IN RANGE, TRADE LETHARGIC.

text.p: Japan rubber futures prices are likely to drift within relatively narrow ranges next week in lethargic summer trading, Japanese traders said.

"There will be little change in the recent sluggish trading pattern as private investors' attention is focused on more volatile commodity futures such as platinum group metals and grains," an analyst at a commodity brokerage said.
Traders expected TOCOM benchmark January rubber to move in a range of about 118 to 125 yen per kg next week ahead of Japan's traditional Obon holidays.
The TOCOM benchmark January contract ended the morning at 120.7 yen per kg, down marginally from 121.3 yen last Friday.
Similarly, the benchmark January contract on the Kobe Rubber Exchange was quoted at 120.8 yen, against 120.9 yen.
Amid a lack of speculative interest in rubber futures, the market was tending to ignore even supportive factors, they said.
"A recent gradual fall in Japan's rubber stocks will not be enough to push up Japanese prices, as there is no concern over supplies," one trader said.
Japan's rubber stocks at designated warehouses at the end of July amounted to 27,569 tonnes, compared with 39,589 tonnes at the end of April, according to the Rubber Trade Association of Japan.

The financial crisis in Thailand, which is calling for the biggest international lending programme since the 1995 Mexican peso crisis, has had a muted impact on the rubber market so far, although the programme is being closely monitored.
With regard to the Japane market, demand from the tyre sector is expected to be strong.

Bridgestone Corp, a leading tyre maker, said this week it had raised its forecast for tyre output in 1997 to a record 570,000 tonnes from an initial estimate of 540,000 tonnes in February, due to better-than-expected tyre exports.
Thai rubber to Japan was offered at 95.00 U.S. cents per kg on an FOB basis on Friday, compared with 96.00 cents on Aug 1.
In the local physical market, benchmark Thai rubber for large-lot end users was quoted at 125.0 yen per kg as of Friday, compared with 127.0 yen a week ago.
